introduction: Cass keeps a post in the yard and shouts at whoever is standing at it. Today that is you. No magnifying glass, no moderator, no score — one question, twice over: which of these three lines actually answers her?
introductionSummary: A practice bout at Cass's post. She throws the lines Tobias will throw on Sunday, and you find the one that answers them.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Answering the animal instead of the argument. Six weeks, a bin, a tail: all facts about somebody, none of them facts about the pond.

sentences.text: Easy one first. I am the yard, and the yard has had a think about you.
You have been here six weeks, Rue. Six weeks does not buy you an opinion about our water.

opponentPrompt.summary: Cass plays the yard and tells him six weeks is not long enough to have earned a view about the water.

options.reason: You answered an Ad Hominem with an Ad Hominem. There are now two attacks on the floor and still nothing at all about the water.
options.summary: You hit back at her tail, and the exchange becomes a contest about which of you counts less.

sentences.text: And you have been here long enough that nobody will hear a word out of you, so I am not sure either of us is winning.

logicalFallacies.explanation: It answers a remark about Rue with a remark about Cass. Both are about animals; neither is about the pond.

options.reason: True, and beside the point. Correcting the number concedes that the number was the question.
options.summary: You correct the arithmetic, which quietly agrees that time served is what the argument is about.

sentences.text: Six weeks and two days, actually. I have been counting.

options.reason: Names the swap — the line was about you, the question is about the water — and then moves the floor onto something anybody present can go and check.
options.summary: You refuse the trade and put the drain in front of her instead, where anyone can go and look.

sentences.text: How long I have been here does not change what is in the pond. Come to the outflow with me and tell me I am wrong about the grate.
Good sting. Terrible answer. You have just agreed the whole thing is a contest about who we are, and you will lose that one — they are prettier than you and there are more of them.

statement.summary: She enjoys the sting and points out he has agreed to fight on the one ground where he is outnumbered.

sentences.text: Two days. Marvellous. Now the whole yard is arguing about the calendar and not one animal is looking at the drain.

statement.summary: She lets the correction stand and notes that the argument is now about dates rather than about the drain.

sentences.text: That is it. You did not defend yourself, you made me look at the drain. Never defend yourself, Rue. Redirect.

statement.summary: She approves: he did not defend himself, he moved her attention to the thing that can be checked.

sentences.text: Harder. This one is Tobias's favourite, so listen to how soft it is.
Nobody blames you, dear. It is simply that an animal who eats out of a bin cannot be expected to mind what is in the water. It is not personal.
He has just told the whole farm your evidence does not count, and he has made it sound like weather. Answer him.

opponentPrompt.summary: She hands him Tobias's gentlest line — the bin, offered as sympathy — and points out what it quietly does.

options.reason: A remark about a group, answered with a remark about a group. The drain has left the room and nobody noticed it go.
options.summary: You answer a slur about bins with a slur about donkeys, and the pond drops out of the conversation.

sentences.text: Says the donkey. You lot stand in that water for an hour every morning and I have seen what happens next.

logicalFallacies.explanation: It swaps one group of animals for another. Neither sentence is a claim about what is actually fouling the pond.

options.reason: It was rude, and you are owed the apology. But now the debate is about his manners rather than about whether your bin has anything to do with the water.
options.summary: You ask for an apology, which puts his manners on the floor in place of the pond.

sentences.text: That is a rude thing to say to somebody's face and I would like an apology for it.

options.reason: Finds the soft Ad Hominem inside a polite sentence and turns it into a question that can actually be settled by going and looking.
options.summary: You unwrap the polite version — it is still about what you are — and ask for pawprints, offering the grate in return.

sentences.text: It sounds kind, but it is still a claim about what I am rather than about what happened. If my bin is fouling the pond, show me the trail. I will show you the bent grate.
Now it is donkeys against raccoons and nothing is getting fixed. He would let you win that one, and you would still lose the vote.

statement.summary: She points out that a fight between kinds is one Tobias would happily concede and still win.

sentences.text: You will get your apology. He is magnificent at apologies. You will also get the trough by the road.

statement.summary: She promises the apology will be beautiful and will change nothing about where he drinks.

sentences.text: Good. He dresses it up, so you undress it. What I am, against what happened. Say that in front of Duchess and she will write it down, and she writes down very little.

statement.summary: She approves and says the phrase is worth using in front of the moderator, who records almost nothing.
